items.title: D-REAL: Acceptance-Length Optimization with Unbiased Gradients for Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoding efficiency depends on the number of consecutively accepted draft tokens, yet token-level training objectives do not directly optimize this quantity. We introduce D-REAL (Drafter Reinforcement of E...
items.editor_note: Opens the thread: trains the drafter on consecutive accepted tokens with unbiased gradients instead of token-level loss.

items.title: D3Tree: Learning to Prune Block-Diffusion Draft Trees for Efficient Verification
items.summary_1line: Block-diffusion drafters propose a whole block of tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees built from their position-wise marginals increase the expected accepted length of speculative decoding. Every tree node occupies a query row in target verification, so under concurrent s
items.editor_note: Names the cost of big draft trees under concurrency: every node takes a verification row, so it learns to prune them.

items.title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoding speeds up language models by letting a lightweight drafter propose several future tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Block diffusion drafters such as DFlash draft a whole block in one forward pass, and DDTree builds a draft tree from their per
items.editor_note: Extends block-diffusion drafting (DFlash, DDTree) with fork-aware draft trees.

items.title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is o
items.editor_note: Questions the shared design of Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark by drafting phrases against a frozen target.

items.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by having a draft model propose multiple tokens for the target model to verify in one pass. The speedup is governed by the expected acceptance length (EAL), yet standard...
items.editor_note: Second acceptance-length objective in four days, framed as optimizing expected acceptance length directly.

items.title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
items.summary_1line: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding. We present Callo, a disaggregated serving system that leverage...
items.editor_note: First serving-system entry: speculates on agent requests whose KV cache was invalidated by context edits.

items.title: PACD: Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding for Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations in Omnimodal Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Omnimodal large language models (Omni-LLMs) integrate audio, video, and text for multimodal reasoning, yet remain vulnerable to cross-modal hallucinations, where one modality improperly influences predictions about an...
items.editor_note: Adjacent: consensus decoding against cross-modal hallucination in omnimodal models, not a speedup method.

items.title: LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
items.summary_1line: Looped Transformers achieve large effective depth with compact models by repeatedly applying a weight-shared block across R recurrent steps, each maintaining a loop-specific key-value (KV) cache. To accelerate sequent...
items.editor_note: Adapts long-context self-speculative decoding to looped Transformers with per-loop KV caches.

items.title: DistDNA: Language Model Fingerprinting under Stochastic Decoding
items.summary_1line: Behavioral fingerprints identify a large language model (LLM) from its responses to a shared set of prompts, enabling applications such as verifying whether a deployed model corresponds to the checkpoint it claims to be. Deployed models, however, are commonly served with stochast
items.editor_note: Adjacent: model fingerprinting that survives stochastic decoding, relevant to verifying which checkpoint is served.

items.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
items.summary_1line: Introduces DICE, a speculative decoding method that pre-samples verification randomness and uses it with an existing drafter to direct drafting toward likely continuations, reporting throughput gains of up to 24.6pp over baselines.
items.editor_note: Shows verification randomness can be pre-sampled and fed to the drafter, reporting up to 24.6pp throughput gains.

items.title: Grammar-as-a-Draft: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs
items.summary_1line: Introduces Grammar-as-a-Draft (GaaD), which merges grammar-forced tokens into speculative decoding draft rows for JSON, regex, and tool-call outputs, raising acceptance length and decoding speed in vLLM and Rust runtimes on TPU v7x.
items.editor_note: First result aimed at agent output formats: grammar-forced tokens raise acceptance length for JSON, regex and tool calls in vLLM.

items.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Contrastive Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Introduces CONCOR, a controlled benchmark that scores how contrastive decoding methods rank ground-truth objects against hallucinated candidates in multimodal LLMs, using a Contrastive Grounding Margin metric.
items.editor_note: Adjacent: a benchmark for evaluating contrastive decoding against multimodal hallucination.

items.title: Look Back, Draft Ahead: Corrective Prefix Attention for Parallel Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Introduces Corrective Prefix Attention, a parallel speculative decoding method that lets draft tokens attend to earlier choices in the block, reporting 13–15% more committed tokens per round than DSpark and up to 3.37× mean speedup on Qwen3 targets.
items.editor_note: Lets parallel draft tokens attend to earlier choices in the block, up to 3.37x mean speedup on Qwen3 targets.

items.title: Pando: Noise-Coupled Parallel Draft Trees for Efficient Edge Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Pando is a speculative decoding method that builds dynamic draft trees on a parallel drafter using noise-coupled pruning, reporting 5.3x speedup and 4.2x energy reduction over autoregressive decoding for a 16-node tree on an edge device.
items.editor_note: Takes draft trees to edge devices, reporting 5.3x speedup and 4.2x lower energy for a 16-node tree.

items.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
items.summary_1line: LEGOSpec is a modular framework that splits speculative decoding draft models into four swappable components and trains them under matched conditions, yielding the DFlux draft that improves acceptance length on Qwen and Gemma models.
items.editor_note: Splits drafters into four swappable parts trained under matched conditions, producing the DFlux draft.

items.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
items.summary_1line: The paper applies post-hoc calibration, mainly standard temperature scaling, to the draft model in speculative decoding, reporting acceptance length gains of up to about 10% with almost no added cost across tasks.
items.editor_note: Cheapest upgrade in the thread: post-hoc temperature scaling of the draft for up to about 10% longer acceptance.

items.title: FlyingStart: Learned Cross-Token Warm Starts for Fixed-Point Decoding in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
items.summary_1line: FlyingStart is a linear warm start, fitted in closed form on a frozen model, that predicts each token's fixed point from the previous token's stopping state, cutting decoding layers by 14–19% on Huginn-0125.
items.editor_note: Adjacent: closed-form warm starts cut decoding layers 14–19% in recurrent-depth models, without a drafter.

items.title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
items.summary_1line: DFly2 is a block-parallel speculative decoding drafter that reuses the target model's KV cache and per-query sparse index selections instead of keeping its own cache, and it accepts more tokens per step than DFlash and DSpark.
items.editor_note: Latest entry: the drafter reuses the target's KV cache and sparse index selections instead of keeping its own.

editorial.tldr: Early November papers reworked the drafter: acceptance-length losses (D-REAL, REAL Loss) and pruned or fork-aware block-diffusion draft trees. By Nov 20 the work reached serving and real output formats, with Callo decoding on invalidated KV and Grammar-as-a-Draft speeding JSON and tool-call outputs in vLLM.
editorial.whats_new: DFly2 (Nov 25) drops the drafter's own KV cache and reuses the target's cache and sparse index selections, accepting more tokens per step than DFlash and DSpark on long contexts.
editorial.why_it_matters: Long-context agent traffic makes a separate drafter cache a memory cost; DFly2-style sharing and grammar-forced drafting target the workloads platform teams actually serve, not chat benchmarks.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agents emit JSON or tool calls, benchmark grammar-forced drafting on your vLLM structured-output path first, and try temperature-calibrating your existing draft model before swapping drafters.

beats.headline: D-REAL and REAL Loss train drafters on expected acceptance length
beats.summary: Both argue token-level objectives miss the number that sets the speedup, consecutive accepted draft tokens, and optimize it directly.

beats.headline: Three papers rework how block-diffusion and phrase drafters propose tokens
beats.summary: D3Tree prunes draft trees to save verification rows, DForkTree builds fork-aware trees from DFlash-style drafters, and a phrase-level drafter proposes beyond the target's vocabulary.

beats.headline: Speculation moves into serving systems and looped models
beats.summary: Callo decodes agent requests whose KV cache was invalidated before re-prefill finishes; LoopCache adapts self-speculation to per-loop KV caches.

beats.headline: Grammar-as-a-Draft and DICE target structured outputs and verification randomness
beats.summary: GaaD merges grammar-forced tokens into draft rows for JSON, regex and tool-call outputs in vLLM; DICE pre-samples verification randomness to steer an existing drafter.

beats.headline: Cheap drafter upgrades: calibration, prefix attention, edge trees, modular training
beats.summary: Temperature-scaling the draft adds up to about 10% acceptance length, Corrective Prefix Attention commits 13–15% more tokens than DSpark, Pando reports 5.3x on edge, and LEGOSpec yields the DFlux draft.

beats.headline: Non-speculative decoding papers clustered into the thread
beats.summary: Hallucination-mitigation decoding, fingerprinting under stochastic decoding, and recurrent-depth warm starts share vocabulary but not the draft-verify mechanism.

beats.headline: DFly2 shares the target's KV cache and sparsity with the drafter
beats.summary: A block-parallel drafter with no cache of its own, aimed at long-context decoding, beating DFlash and DSpark on accepted tokens per step.

open_questions: Does Callo's decode-on-invalidated-KV approach ship in an open serving stack such as vLLM or SGLang, or stay a research prototype?
Do acceptance-length losses like D-REAL and REAL Loss show up in released EAGLE-3 or DFlash drafter checkpoints?
Does Grammar-as-a-Draft land upstream in vLLM's structured-output path, and on GPUs as well as TPU v7x?
Does DFly2's shared-cache drafter release code, and how much memory does it save against a separate drafter cache at long context?
Do the November drafter gains hold against production serving baselines rather than each paper's own suite?
